question: Under the Terms and Conditions of Belfius Bank's EUR 25 billion EMTN Programme, can a Noteholder declare its Notes immediately repayable if Belfius fails to pay principal or interest when due, and which event does give holders that acceleration right?
reference_answer: No. A payment default on principal or interest that continues for 30 days or more after the due date only allows a holder to institute proceedings for the dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer in Belgium; it does not by itself allow acceleration. The right to give written notice to the Paying Agent that the Notes are immediately repayable (Event of Default Redemption Amount plus, if applicable, accrued interest) arises only in the event of a dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer under Belgian law, including bankruptcy, judicial liquidation or voluntary liquidation (other than a voluntary liquidation in connection with a reconstruction, merger or amalgamation where the continuing corporation assumes all liabilities of the Issuer). Resolution action by the Relevant Resolution Authority does not entitle holders to accelerate.

evidence.text: If default is made in the payment of any principal or interest due in respect of the Subordinated Notes or the Senior Notes and such default continues for a period of 30 days or more after the due date, any holder of the relevant Notes may institute proceedings for the dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer in Belgium. In the event of a dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, bankruptcy (faillissement/faillite), judicial liquidation (gerechtelijke vereffening/liquidation forcée) or voluntary liquidation (vrijwillige vereffening/liquidation volontaire) (other than a voluntary liquidation in connection with a reconstruction, merger or amalgamation where the continuing corporation assumes all liabilities of the Issuer) under the laws of Belgium, each holder of Notes of the relevant Series of Notes may give written notice to the Paying Agent at its specified office that its relevant Note(s) is (are) immediately

repayable, whereupon the Event of Default Redemption Amount of such Note(s) together (if applicable) with accrued interest to the date of payment shall become immediately due and payable. … shall not entitle the holders of the relevant Notes to accelerate the Issuer’s payment obligations thereunder.

question_natural: Can Belfius EMTN noteholders accelerate their Notes after a missed payment, and what event triggers acceleration?

question: According to the fees and expenses section of the consolidated Prospectus for Germany of Guggenheim Global Investments plc dated 9 November 2023, what maximum fees may the Administrator and the Depositary charge each Fund (as a percentage of Net Asset Value), what minimum annual fee applies to the Administrator, and what is the cap on the Directors' aggregate remuneration?
reference_answer: The Administrator may charge up to 0.05% per annum of each Fund's Net Asset Value, subject to a minimum fee of $50,000 (USD) per annum. The Depositary may charge up to 0.023% per annum of each Fund's Net Asset Value, under a tiered arrangement in which actual fees fall as a Fund's NAV grows (and subject to certain minimum amounts for small Funds), plus transaction and sub-custodian charges. The Directors' aggregate remuneration will not exceed €114,000 per annum. All fees are stated exclusive of VAT; the investment management and Manager's fees are set in each Fund's Supplement.

evidence.text: all fees and expenses referred to in this section of the Prospectus are exclusive of VAT … The aggregate amount of Directors’ remuneration will not exceed €114,000 per annum. … 10.3 Administrator’s Fee … fee accrued at each Dealing Day and payable monthly in arrears, of up to 0.05 per cent per annum of the Net Asset Value of each Fund subject to a minimum fee of $50,000 per annum.

10.4 Depositary’s Fee The Depositary shall be entitled to receive, out of the assets of each Fund, a fee accrued daily and payable monthly in arrears, of up to 0.023 per cent per annum of the Net Asset Value of each Fund. The Company has negotiated a tiered fee arrangement so that the actual fees charged reduce as the net asset value of the relevant Fund increases.

question: How did the AMF's (Autorité des marchés financiers) net result and its working capital change between the 2024 and 2025 financial years, in € million?
reference_answer: The AMF's net result improved from a net loss of €3.83 million (deficit) in 2024 to a minimal net loss of €0.66 million in 2025, after taking into account a repayment of €7.47 million to the general State budget. Working capital, which is still negative, rose from -€19.03 million in 2024 to -€8.61 million in 2025, thanks to a contribution of €10.42 million to working capital (an improvement of €10.42 million).
